items.title: Effect of Earnings Quality on Stock Valuation
items.venue: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ECONOMICS AND FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT
items.summary: This study examined the effect of earnings quality on stock valuation of listed oil and gas companies in Nigeria, with specific focus on accrual quality and earnings persistence.
items.finding: Earnings persistence, on the other hand, had a positive and significant influence on share price (β = 333.14, p = 0.018), indicating that firms with more sustainable earnings attracted higher market valuation.

items.title: Corporate Bond Multipliers: Substitutes Matter
items.summary: Many economic questions require estimating the price effect of demand shifts (multipliers) in the bond market.
items.finding: Furthermore, we find that the multiplier is larger for high-yield bonds, longer-maturity bonds, and bonds with greater arbitrage risks.

items.title: Optimal Time-Consistent Debt Policies
items.summary: We study a dynamic trade-off model where shareholders can freely adjust debt but lack commitment to future debt policies.
items.finding: This policy has realistic properties and bridges the gap between the static trade-off theory of debt and theory based on the leverage ratchet effect.

items.title: The Coherence Side of Rationality: Theory and Evidence from Firm Plans
items.summary: Using the Duke Survey data on firms’ internal plans, we show that over 80% of Chief Financial Officer (CFO) forecasts align closely with simple heuristics taught in MBA textbooks.
items.finding: Such forecasts are associated with predictable reversals in forecast errors, lower firm performance, and underinvestment.

items.title: Adverse Selection and the Government Intervention Trap
items.summary: But search frictions in asset trading impede efficiency, inviting government intervention.
items.finding: In a dynamic setting, high-quality firms may tolerate current adverse selection when raising financing because they expect future opportunities to profitably acquire assets from failed lower-quality firms.

items.title: Argentina's equity risk around the Milei reforms: a diagnostic decomposition of sovereign, liquidity, behavioral, and institutional premia
items.summary: This study aims to examine how Argentina's required equity returns evolved across four policy regimes between 2015 and 2025, with particular attention to the Milei reform period.
items.finding: Practical implications For investors and policymakers, the evidence suggests that the early rerating of Argentine equities has been driven mainly by lower sovereign risk.

items.title: Investor and Managerial Sentiment and Stock Returns: An Integrative Literature Review of the Evidence, Measurement Approaches, and Emerging-Market Research Agenda
items.venue: International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science
items.summary: Investor sentiment is increasingly becoming a major topic of discussion and analysis within behavioral finance.
items.finding: The findings of the review suggest that market outcomes are connected to investor sentiment and managerial tone.

IMPACT OF ESG INVESTING ON STOCK MARKET PERFORMANCE: A COMPARATIVE STUDY OF SELECTED INDIAN COMPANIES
items.venue: EPRA International Journal of Multidisciplinary Research (IJMR)
items.summary: This study evaluates the relationship between Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) performance and stock market performance among selected Indian companies across diverse sectors.
items.finding: Furthermore, the linear regression model ($R^2 = 0.6516, F = 14.9621, p < 0.05$) indicates that ESG scores account for approximately 65.16% of the variance in long-term stock returns ($Y = -16.1034 + 0.5262X$).

items.title: The Role of Digital Trading Platforms in Promoting Stock Market Participation: A Special Reference to Kerala State
items.publisher: International journal of research and scientific innovation
items.venue: International journal of research and scientific innovation
items.summary: Digital trading platforms significantly drive retail stock market participation by lowering cost barriers, removing geographic restrictions and streamlining user interfaces.
items.finding: Ultimately, digital trading platforms act as a powerful catalyst for financial inclusion, though sustained market stability depends on balanced regulatory oversight and improved investor literacy.
